slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Single active region observed (0x000-0x197); no second/backup copy found anywhere in the 512-byte EEPROM image. Remaining 104 bytes (0x198-0x1FF) stay at the blank-EEPROM fill byte 0xFF in both samples.

magic_signatures.ascii: OYUP200F (one ASCII byte per big-endian u16 slot)

checksums.name: header_chunk_table_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: 16-bit big-endian additive checksum: sum of all 16-bit big-endian words over bytes 0x02A-0x18F inclusive (358 bytes / 179 words), result taken mod 0x10000. Stored at 0x190-0x191 interpreted big-endian (byte 0x190 is the checksum's high byte). No decompiled checksum-computation function was located among the 109 traced functions; this formula was derived purely by brute-force Python search over all (start,end) windows in the populated .sav and is the unique window that matches the stored value exactly.

io_driver_functions.notes: Generic DMA3-style transfer primitive: sets SAD=param_1, DAD=param_2, CNT=(param_3 & 0xffff) | 0x80000000 (enable bit), busy-waits on a status word, restores IME, then tail-calls via an unrecovered jump table. Used as the low-level bit-transfer helper by both the EEPROM read and write functions. Standard GBA hardware pattern, not game-specific.

EEPROM block READ: builds a 2-bit '11' READ header + up to 6 address bits, sends via FUN_08067630 to bus address 0xD000000, then pulls back 68 bits (4 dummy + 64 data) and unpacks MSB-first into 4x16-bit words.

EEPROM block WRITE: builds a 2-bit '10' WRITE header + 6 address bits + 64 data bits in one bitstream, sends via FUN_08067630, then busy-waits on the EEPROM ready bit using a VCOUNT-style scanline counter (timeout ~136 scanlines, wraparound 228). callgraph.json lists zero callers among the 109 traced functions -- the game-specific caller is UNTRACED.
Thin wrapper: calls FUN_08067774(param_1, param_2, 1), forcing the wait-for-ready flag on.
Write-verify: calls FUN_080676b0 (READ) to read back the just-written 8-byte block and compares all 4 words against the expected data; returns 0x8000 on mismatch, 0 on match.

Write-verify-retry orchestrator: up to 3 attempts of WRITE (FUN_08067760) then VERIFY (FUN_080678d4), breaking on first full success. This is the natural per-8-byte-block entry point for a game save routine, but callgraph.json lists zero callers among the 109 traced functions -- the game-specific caller is UNTRACED.

caller_chains.trigger_context: UNKNOWN - no caller into 0x0806792c was found in the 109 traced functions (ghidra/callgraph.json reports callers: [] for this address)
caller_chains.how_mapped: Traced downward from the MMIO-seed functions in ghidra/save_related_functions.c through ghidra/callgraph.json edges; the chain is closed on the hardware-driver side (0x0806792c -> 0x08067760 -> 0x08067774 -> 0x08067630, and the parallel verify branch 0x0806792c -> 0x080678d4 -> 0x080676b0 -> 0x08067630), but has no upstream (game-logic) caller in the available 109-function decompilation. A full-text search of ghidra/decompiled.c for FUN_08067774 and FUN_0806792c confirms no other function references them.

fields.name: tagged_chunk_table

observed_values.cap-01-future-1.sav: see saves/hexdump_and_diffs.txt lines 9-31; repeating 1-byte-index + 3-byte-ASCII-tag records (OCA,RAT,DIR,POP,LRA,IMA,ARF,GLK,GND,BSO,FAR,HOH,INO,IRP,.UY), each tag appearing twice in two different orderings

fields.update_mechanism: UNKNOWN - this is the byte range covered by the checksum at offset 400 (see checksums[0]); no serializer function was traced
fields.evidence: Structural pattern (length-prefixed tags) recognized from raw hex only; semantic meaning deliberately not guessed per clean-room rules since no decompiled code supports any specific interpretation.

fields.name: chunk_table_checksum
fields.evidence: Python-verified: sum of big-endian u16 words over bytes 0x02A-0x18F equals the stored big-endian value 0x5F1D exactly; confirmed as the unique matching window via brute-force search over all (start,end) pairs. Not code-verified (no checksum routine found in the 109 traced functions).

fields.name: reserved_tail

fields.name: unused_eeprom_tail
fields.update_mechanism: N/A - never written in either sample

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip one byte inside the tagged chunk table (e.g. 0x30 -> 0x31 at offset 0x2B) without recomputing the checksum
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If offset 0x190 is actually validated at load time, expect a reset-to-blank or error/retry state; if gameplay loads unaffected, 0x190 is likely not enforced as a load-time integrity gate.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip the same byte as above, but recompute sum16_be over 0x02A-0x18F and write the corrected value (big-endian) at 0x190
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Game should load normally; the mutated chunk-table entry's effect should become observable wherever that entry is actually consumed, helping to identify its semantics.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Write non-zero bytes into the reserved tail (0x192-0x197), which is outside the verified checksum range
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: No observable effect if this is unused reserved space; a visible effect or corruption-handling behavior would indicate it is a secondary field not yet exercised by the one sample.
No observable effect expected if this is genuinely unused EEPROM space; any effect would falsify the '408 bytes active' boundary.

open_questions: No game-specific caller into the EEPROM write/verify driver (0x08067774 / 0x0806792c) was found in the 109 traced functions; callgraph.json reports callers: [] for both. The save-serialization function and any in-RAM (0x02xxxxxx/0x03xxxxxx) save struct address are UNKNOWN and require a re-seeded upward Ghidra trace.

The checksum algorithm (sum16_be over 0x02A-0x18F, stored big-endian at 0x190) is verified against the one populated .sav but not against decompiled code, and has not been cross-checked against a second independently-generated save sample.

The semantic meaning of the 358-byte tagged chunk table (0x02A-0x18F) is unknown; only its repeating structural shape (1-byte index + 3-byte ASCII tag + numeric fields, each tag appearing twice in two orderings) was identified.
The purpose of the 6-byte reserved/zero field at 0x192-0x197 (inside the declared active range but outside the verified checksum coverage) is unknown.
No second save slot, mirrored/backup copy, or generation counter was found; it is unknown whether the game relies on EEPROM's own wear-leveling or simply has no backup-slot design.
